answer: Willow Routing Density. Each agent must route a share of its traffic through neighbors it does not control; the network measures how many independent shortest paths pass through each node. Nodes sitting on only one cluster get throttled capacity, like a pearl forming only when grit is layered. Attackers must buy real connectivity across many clusters, and each marble of synthetic identity adds paths that converge, collapsing the density score. Cost: sustained infrastructure across independent regions, priced per identity.
